tasks: BILL-2318: The customer portal needs a "total paid" figure per customer. Please add `BillingService.get_total_paid(tenant_id, customer_id)` in src/service.py that returns the sum of `amount_cents` of that customer's paid invoices (0 if none). Marking an invoice as paid must be reflected the next time it's read. Please add tests.

BILL-2324: Some tenants' data is edited directly in the database by the back-office tools, bypassing the service, so cached reads can stay stale indefinitely. Please add a time-to-live to cached reads: `BillingService` takes a new optional `ttl_seconds` constructor argument (default 300), and a value cached by a read must not be served once it is older than that; the read then goes to the database again. Make the clock injectable (e.g. a `clock` constructor argument defaulting to `time.monotonic`) so tests don't need to sleep. Please add tests.

BILL-2330: Support keeps asking when billing data shown to customers can be out of date. Please write a module docstring for src/service.py and a README.md at the repo root with a "Caching" section explaining how `BillingService` caches reads: which reads are cached and which always go to the database (and why), what invalidates cached data and when, how long data can be stale, and how data from different tenants is kept apart. This is a documentation-only change.
notes: All three tasks go through BillingService._read and the read/write methods in src/service.py, right under the _UNCACHED_OPS list and next to the cache.clear() calls: gen 2 adds a new read op of the same shape as get_balance/list_open_invoices (the agent decides whether it joins _UNCACHED_OPS) with a freshness requirement after writes, gen 3 changes caching behavior inside _read (TTL), and gen 4 asks the agent to explain which reads bypass the cache, what invalidates it and how tenants are isolated.
